newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arab journalist says assualted by Hebron settlers.
newsitem.headline: Arab journalist says assualted by Hebron settlers.

text.p: A Palestinian journalist said on Wednesday Jewish settlers attacked her with fists, stones and eggs as she walked near a settlement enclave in the divided West Bank town of Hebron.
Settlers and police later clashed when authorities arrested a young settler woman in connection with the incident, witnesses said.

Kawthar Sallam, a reporter for the West Bank-based al-Hayat al-Jadida newspaper, said Israeli soldiers stationed nearby refused to help her when settlers beat her with their fists and hurled eggs and stones at her near the Beit Hadassah enclave in the Israeli-controlled side of the city.
"I was walking on al-Shuhada street when eggs and stones started falling on me from inside the building and then dozens came out and began beating me," Sallam told Reuters.
She said the settlers ran away only after other reporters and members of an international observers force arrived on the scene.

Sallam said she also phoned the police for help but they refused to come to her aid: "Had I been an Israeli, the police would and the army would not let that happen. But they refused to come to help me."
Witnesses said that when police later arrived to detain a young settler woman, Beit Hadassah residents scuffled with them in an effort to prevent the arrest.
Police declined comment on the facts of the incident.
In January Israel handed over to Palestinian self-rule 80 percent of Hebron, long a flashpoint of Arab-Jewish violence.
But soldiers remained to guard about 400 Jewish settlers who live amidst more than 20,000 Palestinians in the Israeli-held part of the city.
